lawyer:
Md. Jani Alam, S. M. Huq ------ For the Appellants.

parties:
Mohar Ali & ors ------ Appellant.
Vs.
Zafar Ali and ors ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 3. The suit was contested by Defendants Nos. 1 to 5 as well as by Defendant Nos. 27 to 48 and 50 to 61 who filed two separate written statements. Defendant Nos. 1 to 5 pleaded inter alia that the suit was not maintainable in the present form and was bad for defect of parties and misjoinder of parties and causes of action and alleged that the genealogy and the sequence of death as given in the plaint were incorrect and that the suit was barred by limitation and adverse possession. The main contention of the said Defendants as stated in their written statement was however that it was true that the suit properties did originally belong to Rajab Ali and that Rajab Ali died leaving behind not only two sons and a widow but also 6 daughters who inherited the suit property but that they being satisfied with the conduct of Defendant Nos. 1 to 5 and dissatisfied with the rude behavior and unkind treatment of Aziz Baksh, relinquished and gave up their -/8/8 gondas share of the disputed land in favour of Jalal Baksh and got the same recorded in the name of Jalal Baksh along with his own share to the knowledge of Aziz Baksh who raised no objection. Thereafter by amicable partition of the suit land by metes and bounds with his brother Aziz Baksh, Jalal Baksh possessed his -/11/4 gondas share of the suit land duly demarcated till his death. After the death of Surati Bibi the share of Jalal Baksh increased to /12/4 gondas share which was also duly demarcated. It is therefore alleged that the suit lands having already been partitioned amicably, there was no scope for further partition.
